The composite is based on polyaniline (PANI) doped with camphorsulfonic acid (CSA) mixed into an epoxy resin matrix.
Numerical simulations using Monte Carlo and modified Dijkstra’s algorithm determined percolation thresholds for PANI, PPy, and PTh as 35.7%, 0.1%, and 38.3% respectively.
PANI was selected due to better mechanical stability and processing properties.
PANI synthesis yield was 63.6%, confirmed by Raman and IR spectroscopy.
PANI/epoxy composites were prepared with PANI volume contents from 20% to 70%; 50% was the maximum for molding.
SEM showed PANI agglomeration at low filler contents and more uniform distribution at higher contents.
Electrical conductivity of 50% PANI composite was 0.440 ± 0.330 S/cm; 30% PANI composite conductivity was below detection but improved after polishing.
Raman spectra revealed doped PANI presence inside the composite but an insulating epoxy shell on the surface.
Mechanical tensile tests showed ultimate tensile strength of 13.75 MPa, about three times lower than typical epoxy.
Thermogravimetric analysis showed composite decomposition temperature at 617.1°C, higher than epoxy’s 500°C.
Numerical thermal simulations indicated heat flux in CF/PANI/epoxy composites during lightning strike was about 1000 times lower than in CFRP.
High-voltage impulse tests with 30% PANI composites showed avalanche breakdown current around 1.062 kA at 15.5 kV charge voltage.
The composite conducts current through the bulk, not just surface currents typical for dielectrics.
The epoxy matrix may form an insulating shell around PANI particles, affecting surface conductivity.
The composite's viscoelastic fracture behavior is typical for duroplastic matrices.
The developed composite could reduce lightning damage extent compared to traditional CFRP with epoxy matrix.
The synthesis involves doping PANI mechanically with CSA in a vibrational mill for 5-15 minutes.
Conductivity of PANI/CSA films was about 6.14 to 7.61 S/cm, independent of mixing time.
The composite aims to replace heavy metallic meshes for lightning strike protection in aircraft.
The study integrates numerical modeling, synthesis, physicochemical, mechanical, thermal characterization, and high-voltage testing.
